pois.name: Dubai Frame Observation Deck
pois.blurb: The Dubai Frame (Arabic: برواز دبي) is an observatory, museum and monument in Zabeel Park, Dubai. It holds the record for the largest frame in the world.

themeConnection.text: The Dubai Frame is a purpose-built landmark structure with a regularly accessible elevated viewing bridge.

pois.name: Empire State Building Observatory
pois.blurb: The Empire State Building is a 102-story, supertall skyscraper in the Midtown South neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City, United States.

themeConnection.text: Public observatories on the 86th and 102nd floors provide panoramic views from New York's landmark skyscraper.

pois.name: Sky100 Hong Kong Observation Deck
pois.blurb: Sky100 (Chinese: 天際100) is a 360-degree indoor observation deck on the 100th floor of the International Commerce Centre, in West Kowloon, Hong Kong, near Kowloon station.

themeConnection.text: Sky100 is a named indoor public observation deck on the 100th floor of the International Commerce Centre.

pois.name: Space Needle Observation Deck
pois.blurb: The Space Needle is an observation tower in Seattle, Washington, United States. Considered to be an icon of the city, it has been designated a Seattle landmark.

themeConnection.text: The Space Needle is a purpose-built landmark observation tower with publicly accessible viewing levels.

pois.name: Shanghai Tower Observation Deck
pois.blurb: The Shanghai Tower is a 128-story, 632-meter-tall (2,073-foot) megatall skyscraper located in Lujiazui, Pudong, Shanghai.

themeConnection.text: Shanghai Tower has a dedicated public observation deck on one of the world's tallest skyscrapers.

pois.name: Skydeck Chicago
pois.blurb: Skydeck Chicago is an observation deck on the 103rd floor of Willis Tower, featuring views of Chicago and glass balconies extending outside the building.

themeConnection.text: Skydeck Chicago is the named public observation deck on the upper floors of Willis Tower.

pois.name: Macau Tower Observation Deck
pois.blurb: Macau Tower has an observation deck at 223 metres and a second outdoor viewing platform, with panoramic views over Macau and the Pearl River.

themeConnection.text: Macau Tower's observation levels are a named, ticketed public viewing venue in the landmark tower.

pois.name: Shibuya Sky
pois.blurb: Shibuya Sky is an observation deck at the top of Shibuya Scramble Square, including an open-air rooftop level with broad views of Tokyo.

themeConnection.text: Shibuya Sky is a named rooftop observation facility atop the Shibuya Scramble Square high-rise.

pois.name: Canton Tower Observation Deck
pois.blurb: Canton Tower is a landmark observation and communications tower with public indoor and outdoor viewing decks overlooking Guangzhou.

themeConnection.text: Canton Tower contains multiple public observation levels in a purpose-built landmark tower.

pois.name: Harukas 300
pois.blurb: Abeno Harukas contains Harukas 300, an observation deck spanning the top three floors and providing 360-degree views across Osaka.

themeConnection.text: Harukas 300 is the named observation facility occupying floors 58 through 60 of Abeno Harukas.

pois.name: Vancouver Lookout
pois.blurb: Vancouver Lookout is an observation deck located atop Harbour Centre in downtown Vancouver, reached by a dedicated glass elevator and open to visitors.

themeConnection.text: Vancouver Lookout is a dedicated public observation deck in the Harbour Centre high-rise.

pois.name: Taipei 101 Observatory
pois.blurb: Taipei 101 has an indoor observation deck on the 89th floor and an outdoor deck on the 91st floor, both offering views of Taipei.

themeConnection.text: Taipei 101 Observatory is a dedicated public viewing facility within the landmark skyscraper.

pois.name: CN Tower Observation Decks
pois.blurb: The CN Tower has public observation facilities including the LookOut Level, Glass Floor, and SkyPod, all designed for panoramic viewing over Toronto.

themeConnection.text: The CN Tower contains several named public viewing levels, including the LookOut Level and SkyPod.

pois.name: KL Tower Observation Deck
pois.blurb: Kuala Lumpur Tower contains public observation facilities including an enclosed observation deck and an open-air Sky Deck high above the city.

themeConnection.text: KL Tower offers dedicated public observation decks in a freestanding landmark telecommunications tower.

pois.name: Tokyo Skytree Tembo Deck
pois.blurb: Tokyo Skytree includes the Tembo Deck at 350 metres and the Tembo Galleria above it, both built as public observation facilities.

themeConnection.text: Tembo Deck is a dedicated public observation level inside the Tokyo Skytree tower.

pois.name: Seoul Sky
pois.blurb: Lotte World Tower contains Seoul Sky, a public observation deck on floors 117 through 123, including a glass-floored viewing area high above Seoul.

themeConnection.text: Seoul Sky is the named public observation facility occupying upper floors of Lotte World Tower.

pois.name: Euromast
pois.blurb: Euromast is an observation tower in Rotterdam, Netherlands, designed by Hugh Maaskant constructed between 1958 and 1960.

themeConnection.text: This landmark observation tower admits the public to panoramic viewing levels above Rotterdam.

pois.name: The View from The Shard
pois.blurb: The Shard, also referred to as the Shard London Bridge and formerly London Bridge Tower, is a 95-storey mixed-use development supertall pyramid-shaped skyscraper, designed by the Italian architect Renzo Piano, in Southwark, London, that forms part of The Shard Quarter…

themeConnection.text: This ticketed public observatory occupies the upper floors of the landmark Shard high-rise in London.

pois.name: Berlin TV Tower Observation Deck
pois.blurb: The Fernsehturm (German: [ˈfɛ͡ənzeːˌtʊ͡ɐm] ; lit. 'Television Tower') in central Berlin was constructed between 1965 and 1969 by the government of the German Democratic Republic as both a functional broadcasting facility and a symbol of communist power.

themeConnection.text: This landmark television tower offers scheduled public admission to its panoramic observation level above Berlin.

pois.name: Melbourne Skydeck
pois.blurb: Eureka Tower is a 297.3 m (975 ft) skyscraper located in the Southbank precinct of Melbourne, Victoria, Australia. Construction began in August 2002 and the exterior was completed on 1 June 2006.

themeConnection.text: This public observation deck occupies the upper levels of the landmark Eureka Tower in Melbourne.

clue.text: Built as the futuristic centerpiece of a 1960s world’s fair themed around the Space Age, this slender tower still sends visitors to a saucer-like observation level above the former fairgrounds.

theme.title: Operating Public Observation Decks in Landmark High-Rises
theme.introduction: Cities reveal a different character from high above. These public observation decks turn skylines into destinations.
theme.inclusionCriteria: Include a location only when every condition is met: (1) it is an individually named, permanent observation deck, observation level, tower observatory, skydeck, or equivalent public viewing venue; (2) the venue is physically located within a high-rise building, freestanding tower, or purpose-built landmark observation structure, with its principal attraction being a panoramic view from an elevated position; (3) it offers regularly scheduled public admission on the date of play, whether ticketed or free, rather than access only through a private event or hotel booking; (4) the named deck or observatory has a fixed, mappable entrance or visitor facility that can be treated as one exact location; (5) the structure lies within the current administrative boundary of a present-day city or incorporated urban municipality; and (6) the venue is identifiable by its own public-facing name or by the name of the tower or high-rise containing it.
